responsibility: Implements the GIMPLE warning pass for problematic uses of alloca and variable-length arrays. Using ranger-derived argument ranges, builtin metadata, loop context, and user-specified size limits, it classifies each allocation as definitely too large, maybe too large, unbounded, zero-sized, or loop-contained, and emits the corresponding -Walloca-larger-than, -Wvla-larger-than, -Walloca, or related diagnostics while supporting a stricter mode that warns only for certain limit violations.
